text: Coconut Fudge Brownies Recipe  Ingredients 1 cup of granulated sugar ½ cup of softened butter, ¼ cup of melted coconut oil and 2 large eggs 1 teaspoon vanilla extract 1 ½ cups all-purpose flour ¾ cup of unsweetened cocoa powder 2 teaspoons baking powder ½ teaspoon salt 1 cup of semisweet chocolate chips ½ cup of shredded coconut  Instructions which are Step 1 Preheat your oven to 350°F (175°C) and line an 8x8 inch baking pan with parchment paper.  Step 2 In a large mixing bowl, cream together the sugar, butter and coconut oil until light and fluffy. Add in the eggs one at a time, beating well after each addition. Stir in the vanilla extract.  Step 3 In another medium sized bowl, whisk together the flour, cocoa powder, baking powder and salt. Gradually add this dry mixture into the wet ingredients, stirring until just combined.  Step 4 Fold in the chocolate chips and shredded coconut until evenly distributed.  Step 5 Pour the batter into the prepared baking pan and smooth out the top using a spatula or the back of a spoon. Bake for 25-30 minutes or until a toothpick inserted into the center comes out clean.  Step 6 Allow the brownies to cool completely before cutting into squares and serving. Enjoy.

Bring to boil, reduce heat, cover and simmer until tender about 20-30 minutes. Strain through a colander, discard solids and use the juice as the base for the soup if desired. Add more filtered water, organic poulet base and season lightly. Add the meat. Put the noodles into a bowl, set the vegetables and place the meat in the center. Put the broth around the edge. Garnish with extra salt, pepper and parsley. Serve immediately.

This paper explores the transition of a three-dimensional (3D) topological insulator, Bi2Se3, to a two-dimensional (2D) state. Utilizing a blend of experimental and theoretical methods, we study Bi2Se3's electronic structure and topological characteristics as its thickness diminishes from 3D to 2D. Our findings reveal that the 3D Dirac cone transforms into a pair of 2D Dirac cones at the edges of the Brillouin zone, leading to the formation of novel topological phases. We find topologically protected edge states on the surfaces of the 2D system which are resilient to disorder and defects. Additionally, we identify non-trivial band structure as well as Fermi arc behavior in the 2D states indicating the presence of non-trivial topology. This research offers new perspectives on the transition of 3D topological insulators to 2D systems and opens avenues for further investigation into low-dimensional topological phenomena.

Medical image segmentation is crucial for clinical analysis and computer aided diagnosis. Unlike 2D images, 3D medical images offer more detailed structures and robust segmentation capabilities. However, effectively utilizing the rich information in 3D medical images is still challenge. This paper introduces UXNet, a novel deep learning architecture for 3D medical image segmentation; UXNet employs a unique upsampled encoder-decoder network with a multi level feature aggregation mechanism. This mechanism enhances the spatial information by upsampling low level features and captures complex structures by aggregating multi level features; UXNet learns more robust representations, improving segmentation accuracy; Extensive experiments on three benchmark datasets including ISLES2017, LLC and SYNAPSE BREAST CT, show that UXNet outperforms state-of-the-art methods. The source code and models are available at https //github.com/CCF-Union/UXNet.

This paper introduces a novel uncertainty aware self ensembling (UA SE) model for 3D left atrium segmentation in semi supervised learning. The UA SE model leverages correlations between neighboring voxels and employs a self ensemble strategy to further strengthen the representation power of semi-supervised learning. Utilizing a 3D residual UNet with an uncertainty estimation module, the model models spatial correlations and outputs an uncertainty map. Additionally, a self ensembling module is proposed that considers both labels and uncertainties by taking into account local graph structure. The model is trained semi-supervisedly, using only a small portion of labeled data for training and leveraging the remaining unlabeled data to enhance its representation power. The proposed method is evaluated on the MICCAI 3D Slicer Tracking Challenge two thousand seventeen dataset; Experimental results show the UA SE model's effectiveness compared to state of the art semi-supervised learning methods. The code and dataset are available at https, //github.com/VITA-Group/UA-SE.

This paper introduces CIDI Lung-Seg, a single-click annotation tool for automatically delineating lungs from CT scans. The tool uses a pre-trained deep learning model to identify and segment the lungs in scans with just a single click; A blinded, controlled study comparing its performance to manual annotation found high agreement (96.2% overall) and a kappa statistic of 0.87. The tool also saves significant time, with an average time saving of 87.2%. This method has the potential to greatly reduce the time required for manual lung cancer annotations.

Delightful Lemon Cake Recipe  Ingredients  2 cups all purpose flour  1 ½ teaspoons baking powder ¼ teaspoon salt -3 large eggs, room temperature  1 cup granulated sugar  2 tablespoons lemon zest, and ¾ cup fresh lemon juice  1 cup buttermilk, room temperature, ½ cup unsalted butter, melted and cooled  2 teaspoons vanilla extract  For the glaze  1 cup powdered sugar -2-3 tablespoons fresh lemon juice  Instructions, Step 1 Preheat your oven to 350°F (175°C) and prepare a 9x13 inch baking pan by greasing it with cooking spray or butter and coating it with flour.  Step 2: In a medium sized bowl, combine the flour, baking powder, and salt. Set aside.  Step 3 In a separate large bowl, beat the eggs and sugar until light and fluffy, about 3 minutes using an electric mixer. Add in the lemon zest and juice and continue mixing until well incorporated.  Step 4 Gradually add the dry ingredients into the wet mixture while alternating with the buttermilk, beginning and ending with the dry ingredients. Mix until just combined.  Step 5 Stir in the melted and cooled butter and vanilla extract until fully mixed.  Step 6 Pour the batter into the prepared baking pan and smooth out the top using a spatula. Bake for 25-30 minutes or until a toothpick inserted into the center comes out clean.  Step 7 Allow the cake to cool completely prior to making the glaze. To make the glaze. Whisk together the powdered sugar and lemon juice in a small bowl until smooth. Drizzle over the cooled cake and let it set for several hours before serving. Enjoy.

Selective Publication in Nature: An Empirical Analysis of Abstracts from the Journal of Statistical Genetics Abstract, We investigate selective publication of papers in Nature Genetics. On one side we analyze the frequency of abstracts in Nature Genetics articles using a logistic regression model, finding significant differences by author, issue and field; No significant difference is observed between journals. On the other hand, we compare publications based on geographic location and type of journal issue (only or top specialization); Similar results are available for consideration; New analyses and possible explanations is under discussion; The first part of the analysis is performed using a logistic regression model. Two hypotheses for potential effects are proposed  -  (i) journals are most often publish manuscripts of the same quality in the same field, and (ii) journals publish only manuscripts with no papers or few original articles. In the second part, we examine manuscripts by author, issue and geographic region. It is shown that patterns differ for abstracts versus no abstracts, controlled for publication status and authorship and geographic location. The study will be discussed at a conference in October two thousand fourteen.

Ingredients 1 cup unsalted butter, softened 1 cup all purpose flour 1 teaspoon baking powder 1/2 teaspoon baking soda 1/4 teaspoon salt 2 cups granulated sugar 1 cup (8 oz) jam (any flavor)  For the Dough Step 1 Preheat the oven to 350 degrees F (175 degrees C). Line a baking sheet with parchment paper. Step 2: In a small bowl whisk together the flour, baking powder, baking soda and salt. Set aside. Step 3 In a large bowl, cream the butter and sugar on medium high speed until light and fluffy, scraping the sides of the bowl as necessary. Beat in the egg and vanilla extract until combined. Gradually add the dry ingredients to the wet ingredients, mixing till just combined. Step 4 For the Filling Step 5 Divide the dough into two equal parts. Roll each portion out on a lightly floured surface to a thickness of 1/4 inch (6 mm). Cut into rounds with a 2-inch (5-cm) cookie cutter. Place half the rounds on the prepared baking sheet. Step 6 Top each round with 1 teaspoon of jam. Place another round on top of the jam, pressing the edges gently to seal. Step 7 Bake for 15 minutes or until the edges are lightly browned. Allow to cool on the baking sheet for 5 minutes before transferring to a wire rack to cool completely. Barry Holmes triumphs in comeback victory  Barry Holmes secured a stunning comeback to win the Welsh Open snooker title in Cardiff. The world number 39 trailed 6-2 to Mark Selby in the final but won eight of the next nine frames to triumph 10-7.  It is the first ranking event success for the 41-year old from Birmingham who has now earned £200,000 in prize money this season.  "I'm over the moon it's been a great week," Holmes said. "I've been working hard on my game and it's nice to get some reward for it."  Selby, the world number two, had been in dominant form throughout the tournament and looked on course for victory when he moved 6-2 ahead. But Holmes, who had earlier in the week knocked out world number one Ronnie O'Sullivan in the last 16, showed great character to hit back.  He levelled at 6-6 with a break of one hundred six and then took the lead for the first time in the match with a run of 70. Selby responded with a break of 77 to make it 7-7, but Holmes took the next three frames moving forward with within one of victory.  The Leicester player then had a chance to force a decider in the 17th frame, but missed a red with the rest when on 46; Holmes made no mistake with a break of 53 to secure the title.  "I'm gutted to lose but I've got to take my hat off to Barry, he played unbelievable," Selby said. "I had my chances in the match, but I couldn't take them. I'm sure I'll be back stronger for it."
